prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1384; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle was turning left and was struck by oncoming vehicle proceeding straight. Insured reports the other driver ran a late yellow. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck strain following impact and is seeking medical evaluation. No attorney on file for claimant.

Entry 2: Spoke with insured by phone. Insured confirms they were completing a left turn when the collision occurred. Insured states visibility of oncoming traffic was partially blocked by a delivery van stopped in the adjacent lane. Photos of both vehicles received and added to file. Dashcam footage requested from insured.

Entry 3: Contacted claimant by phone. Claimant reports stiffness and pain in the neck and upper shoulders, with headaches since the collision. Claimant has seen a primary care provider and is scheduled for follow-up. Claimant is not represented by counsel and asked how the claim process works. Explained coverage terms and the documentation needed for the injury portion of the claim.

Entry 4: Reviewed dashcam footage submitted by the other driver's carrier. Footage shows the oncoming vehicle entering the intersection as the signal changed to red, with the insured's vehicle already partially across the lane. Liability assessment under review. Preliminary view places majority of fault on the oncoming driver, pending police report and witness statement.

Entry 5: Received medical records from claimant's provider. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain with recommended physical therapy. Claimant confirmed by phone they are attending sessions. Reserve adjusted to reflect injury treatment. Liability position updated to reflect dashcam evidence. File remains open pending final medical report and police findings.
